text: The SI unit of force is:

options.whyIncorrect: Joule is the SI unit of work/energy (1 J = 1 N·m).
Watt is the unit of power (J/s).
Pascal is the unit of pressure (N/m²).

explanation: Force = mass × acceleration; 1 newton (N) is the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s². CGS unit: dyne (1 N = 10⁵ dyne).
source: NCERT Class 8–9 Science, Force and Laws of Motion
examRelevance: Units of physical quantities are a staple question.

text: A ball thrown vertically upwards has, at its highest point:
textHi: ऊर्ध्वाधर ऊपर फेंकी गई गेंद के उच्चतम बिंदु पर:

options.whyIncorrect: Acceleration due to gravity (g ≈ 9.8 m/s² downward) acts throughout the flight.

options.text: Zero velocity but acceleration equal to g (downward)

options.whyIncorrect: Velocity is maximum at the point of release, not at the top.
Reversed — velocity is zero, acceleration is g.

explanation: At the highest point, the ball momentarily stops (v = 0) before reversing direction, but gravity continues to act, so acceleration remains g downward. Potential energy is maximum and kinetic energy zero at this point.
source: NCERT Class 9 Science, Motion and Gravitation
examRelevance: Conceptual motion question — tests understanding beyond formulas.

textHi: ध्वनि किसमें संचरण नहीं कर सकती?

options.whyIncorrect: Sound travels in water (~1480 m/s) — faster than in air.
Sound travels fastest in solids like steel (~5000 m/s).
Sound travels in air at about 343 m/s (at 20 °C).

explanation: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave and needs a material medium. In vacuum there are no particles to vibrate, so no sound (the bell-jar experiment). Speed order: solids > liquids > gases. Light, an electromagnetic wave, does travel through vacuum.

text: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles, and why?
textHi: वाहनों में पीछे देखने के दर्पण के रूप में कौन सा दर्पण प्रयोग होता है और क्यों?

options.text: Concave mirror — it magnifies distant objects
options.whyIncorrect: Concave mirrors give inverted/varying images for distant objects; unsuitable for rear view.

options.text: Convex mirror — it gives an erect, diminished image with a wider field of view
Plane mirror — it gives a same-size image
options.whyIncorrect: Plane mirrors have a narrow field of view.

options.text: Convex mirror — it forms real, inverted images
options.whyIncorrect: Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect images.

explanation: Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, diminished images regardless of object distance and cover a wide field of view — ideal for rear-view mirrors and at blind turns. Concave mirrors are used in torches, shaving mirrors and by dentists.
source: NCERT Class 10 Science, Light — Reflection and Refraction
examRelevance: Uses of mirrors — 'science in daily life' type item.

text: Deficiency of which vitamin causes night blindness?
textHi: किस विटामिन की कमी से रतौंधी होती है?

options.whyIncorrect: B1 (thiamine) deficiency causes beri-beri.
Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.
Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets (children) and osteomalacia (adults).

explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) is needed for rhodopsin in rod cells; deficiency → night blindness, xerophthalmia. Sources: carrot, papaya, green leafy vegetables, milk, fish liver oil. Other pairs: B12 — pernicious anaemia; K — bleeding disorder; B3 — pellagra.
source: NCERT Class 6 Science, Components of Food
examRelevance: Vitamin–deficiency disease matching is asked almost every year.

text: Which disease is caused by a protozoan and spread by the female Anopheles mosquito?
textHi: कौन सा रोग प्रोटोजोआ से होता है और मादा एनाफिलीज मच्छर द्वारा फैलता है?

options.whyIncorrect: Dengue is viral and spread by Aedes aegypti.
TB is bacterial (Mycobacterium tuberculosis), airborne.
Typhoid is bacterial (Salmonella typhi), water/food-borne.

explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium (protozoan) transmitted by female Anopheles. Dengue/chikungunya — Aedes; filaria/Japanese encephalitis — Culex. Ronald Ross established the mosquito link (Nobel 1902).
source: NCERT Class 8–9 Science, Microorganisms; Why Do We Fall Ill

text: The direct change of a solid into vapour without passing through the liquid state is called:
textHi: ठोस का द्रव अवस्था में जाए बिना सीधे वाष्प में बदलना क्या कहलाता है?

options.whyIncorrect: Evaporation is liquid → gas at the surface below boiling point.
Condensation is gas → liquid.
Fusion is melting (solid → liquid).

explanation: Sublimation: solid ⇌ gas directly. Examples: camphor, naphthalene balls, dry ice (solid CO₂), iodine, ammonium chloride. Used in separating mixtures like salt and ammonium chloride.
source: NCERT Class 9 Science, Matter in Our Surroundings

text: The powerhouse of the cell, where cellular respiration produces ATP, is the:
textHi: कोशिका का 'ऊर्जा घर', जहाँ कोशिकीय श्वसन से ATP बनता है, है:

options.whyIncorrect: Ribosomes synthesise proteins.
The nucleus controls the cell and contains DNA.
Chloroplasts perform photosynthesis in plant cells ('kitchen of the cell').

explanation: Mitochondria (double membrane, own DNA) carry out aerobic respiration releasing energy stored as ATP. Plant cells additionally have chloroplasts and a cell wall (cellulose) and a large central vacuole.
source: NCERT Class 8–9 Science, Cell — Structure and Functions
examRelevance: Cell organelle functions are frequently tested.

text: Which gas is the main contributor to the greenhouse effect from human activities?
textHi: मानवीय गतिविधियों से ग्रीनहाउस प्रभाव में मुख्य योगदान देने वाली गैस है:

options.whyIncorrect: N₂ (78% of air) is not a greenhouse gas.
O₂ is not a greenhouse gas.
Argon is an inert noble gas, not a greenhouse gas.

explanation: CO₂ from fossil-fuel burning and deforestation is the largest anthropogenic greenhouse gas; methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide (N₂O), CFCs and water vapour also contribute. CFCs additionally deplete the ozone layer (Montreal Protocol 1987; World Ozone Day 16 Sept).
source: NCERT Class 9 Science, Natural Resources; Class 7 Air
examRelevance: Environment topic — greenhouse gases, ozone are recurrent.

text: Why does a pressure cooker cook food faster?
textHi: प्रेशर कुकर में खाना जल्दी क्यों पकता है?

options.text: It traps steam, raising pressure and thus the boiling point of water above 100 °C
It lowers the boiling point of water
options.whyIncorrect: Lower boiling point (as at high altitude) makes cooking SLOWER.
Faster cooking actually saves fuel.

options.text: The metal conducts heat directly into food
options.whyIncorrect: Conduction happens in any metal pot; the pressure effect is what speeds cooking.

explanation: Boiling point rises with pressure. Inside a cooker, pressure ~2 atm raises water's boiling point to ~120 °C, so food cooks faster. Conversely, at hill stations lower pressure lowers the boiling point and cooking takes longer.
source: NCERT Class 9 Science — Matter (effect of pressure on boiling point)

text: The normal human body temperature is approximately:
textHi: सामान्य मानव शरीर का तापमान लगभग होता है:

options.whyIncorrect: 40 °C indicates a high fever.
35 °C is hypothermia threshold.
42 °C is a life-threatening temperature; also the maximum on a clinical thermometer.

explanation: Normal body temperature is about 37 °C = 98.6 °F. A clinical thermometer reads 35–42 °C. Conversion: F = (9/5)C + 32.

text: Photosynthesis in plants primarily takes place in the presence of sunlight using:
textHi: पौधों में प्रकाश संश्लेषण सूर्य के प्रकाश की उपस्थिति में मुख्यतः किसका उपयोग करता है?

options.text: Carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen
Oxygen and water, releasing carbon dioxide
options.whyIncorrect: That describes respiration, not photosynthesis.
Nitrogen is not a raw material of photosynthesis.
Glucose is a product, not a raw material.

explanation: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → (sunlight, chlorophyll) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Occurs in chloroplasts; stomata take in CO₂; oxygen released comes from splitting water.
source: NCERT Class 7 Science, Nutrition in Plants
examRelevance: Foundational biology — frequently asked and also relevant to EVS pedagogy.
